title: What If the World's Fourth-Largest Lake Vanished?

scenes.text: What if the world's fourth-largest lake vanished? One did, within a single lifetime.
The Aral Sea once filled the Central Asian steppe. Then, in the 1960s, the Soviet Union diverted its two rivers to irrigate cotton.
With the rivers cut off, the water shrank year after year, and what was left grew saltier.
Fishing towns lost their living. The old seabed turned to dust laced with fertilizer and pesticides.
Without the lake to soften the weather, winters turned colder, and summers turned hotter and drier.
By 2014, the eastern half of the southern sea was completely gone. Yet a dam finished in 2005 let the northern sea rebound.
